source: solana-developers/program-examples tokens/escrow/anchor (main, MIT), built with Anchor 0.31.1: bench/real/o_escrow
about: Open-source program, unmodified logic: the clean build is expected to have no finding; each variant removes exactly one validation and expects one of its rules at its instruction. Scored for rules only.

why.maker: Signer (pays the offer and vault rent, signs the deposit transfer).
why.token_mint_a / token_mint_b: InterfaceAccount<Mint> owned by token_program (mint::token_program). Any mints: the maker chooses what to trade.
why.maker_token_account_a: associated_token (mint_a, maker, token_program); the TransferChecked CPI needs the maker's signature anyway.
why.offer: init at PDA [offer, maker, id]: fresh, bound to the maker; stores maker, both mints, wanted amount, bump.
why.vault: init as ATA(offer, mint_a, token_program): the offer PDA is its authority.
why.associated_token_program / token_program: Program<AssociatedToken>, Interface<TokenInterface> (SPL Token or Token-2022 only), Program<System>.

why.taker: Signer: pays the wanted tokens (TransferChecked with the taker as authority) and the init_if_needed rent. Permissionless by design: anyone may take an open offer.
why.maker: SystemAccount; offer has_one = maker and the offer PDA seeds use maker.key(): the real maker receives the offer rent (close = maker) and the vault rent.
why.token_mint_a / token_mint_b: offer has_one = token_mint_a / token_mint_b: the mints the maker asked for.
why.taker_token_account_a: init_if_needed ATA(taker, mint_a): the taker receives the vault tokens into its own ATA.
why.taker_token_account_b: ATA(taker, mint_b), mut; the token program requires the taker's signature.
why.maker_token_account_b: init_if_needed ATA(maker, mint_b): the payment goes to the maker.
why.offer: PDA [offer, maker, offer.id] with bump offer.bump, has_one maker / token_mint_a / token_mint_b, close = maker (discriminator zeroed by Anchor's close).
why.vault: ATA(offer, mint_a, token_program): the offer's own vault, emptied and closed with the offer PDA's signature.

why.maker: Signer, and offer has_one = maker + PDA seeds with maker.key(): only the offer's maker can refund.
why.maker_token_account_a: ATA(maker, mint_a): the refund goes back to the maker.
why.offer: PDA [offer, maker, offer.id] / offer.bump, has_one maker / token_mint_a, close = maker.

take_no_mint_b.impact: The taker pays with a worthless mint of its own (token_mint_b, both mint-B ATAs derived from it, init_if_needed creates the maker's) and still receives the whole vault of mint A: theft of every open offer. Nothing else binds token_mint_b to the offer (the ATA constraints only relate the token accounts to whatever mint is passed).

verified.analysis: no check found only in the clean build

take_dest_unbound.removed: maker_token_account_b: associated_token::authority = maker (the ATA binding to the maker; Anchor's ATA init needs it, so the account becomes mut + token::mint = token_mint_b + token::token_program, no init_if_needed)
take_dest_unbound.impact: The taker passes a mint-B token account of its own as maker_token_account_b: the payment goes back to the taker and the vault of mint A still goes to the taker: theft of every open offer. The token program only checks the destination's mint, not its owner.

idl.refund_offer: maker:w token_mint_a maker_token_account_a:w offer:w vault:w token_program

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: maker.signer; in the variant only: maker.owner
verified.note: the maker's try_accounts call (first of the handler's accounts function, bundle/refund_offer.ts) is try_accounts_4258 = Signer::try_accounts in the clean build (security/refund_offer.md: maker signer found via it) and try_accounts_1d0 in the variant, in which only an owner check (SystemAccount: owned by the system program) is found; the other try calls (338, 280, 43c0, 280, 120) are the same functions.

refund_no_signer.impact: Anyone can cancel any open offer (the vault tokens go back to the maker's ATA, the rent to the maker): unauthorized cancellation of other users' orders (denial of service / forced exit, no theft). has_one = maker and the seeds only bind the key, and the vault transfer is signed by the offer PDA, so no other check requires the maker's signature.

discarded.reason: redundant: the offer PDA seeds [offer, maker.key(), id] with the stored bump already bind the offer to the maker account passed.

not exploitable for gain: the vault must be ATA(offer, token_mint_a), so with another mint the taker can only pass an ATA of the offer for that mint (which it funded itself); it still pays the maker the full mint-B price, and the real vault stays locked under the closed offer: the maker ends up with exactly the trade it asked for, the taker only loses. Left out as not clearly security-relevant.
redundant: the PDA seeds bind the offer to maker.key().
redundant: has_one = maker plus the owner / discriminator of Account<Offer> identify the offer; the vault is derived from the offer key.
redundant: the deposit is a TransferChecked with the maker as authority, which the token program only accepts from the account's owner (or delegate).
harmless: only the maker (signer, has_one) can refund, so the destination is the maker's own choice.
redundant: the taker is the authority of the mint-B TransferChecked and the init_if_needed payer, both of which require its signature at the runtime / token program.

redundant: the vault must be ATA(offer, mint_a, token_program) and InterfaceAccount<TokenAccount> requires an SPL Token / Token-2022 owner, so a fake token program cannot be paired with the real vault.
